query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of yttrium to a Zr-based metallic glass alloy will enhance its glass-forming ability by reducing the critical cooling rate required for glass formation.
generation.intervention: addition of 1-3 at.% yttrium to the alloy
generation.conditions: rapid cooling at a rate of 10^4 K/s
generation.mechanism: the addition of yttrium will disrupt the atomic packing structure, leading to a more disordered and stable glassy state
generation.predicted_outcome: a 20-30% reduction in the critical cooling rate required for glass formation, from 10^4 K/s to 7-8 x 10^3 K/s
generation.boundary: yttrium content above 5 at.% may lead to the formation of crystalline phases, negating the glass-forming ability enhancement
generation.uncertainty: the exact mechanism of yttrium's effect on glass-forming ability is not fully understood and may depend on other factors such as alloy composition and cooling rate
